documents.title: Bengaluru Metro: tax estimates, land handovers and foreign-debt support
documents.text: Did corrective procurement and land-readiness controls remove the audited sources of cost escalation before further contract and debt-service commitments? A newly tabled August 2026 audit connects project estimates, contractor claims, land acquisition and international borrowing. Its observations mostly concern progress through March 2023; the missing current action-taken record is central to judging whether the problems persist. CAG §5.1.2 finds ₹1,098.28 crore of taxes remained in estimates for nine civil contracts although bids excluded those taxes; including quoted net premium, the audit calculated ₹1,222.40 crore higher contract prices. This is an audit calculation, not a minister-payment trail. The audit records land-handover delays of 12–1,305 days beyond the allowed 90 days in 13 contracts. Five contractors claimed ₹98.21 crore; ₹12.19 crore had been paid on one claim at the audit snapshot. Claims and payments must remain separate. BMRCL disclosed loans from JICA, AFD, EIB and AIIB as well as domestic institutions and bonds. The audit describes reliance on Karnataka to service external debt as of March 2023, linking project-delivery performance to the state's fiscal burden. Counterevidence: BMRCL replied that bidders priced independently and tender estimates were guidance. CAG disagreed because estimates informed qualification and price reasonableness; BMRCL acknowledged procurement-manual and estimation-SOP recommendations. BMRCL attributed some land-cost increases to additional land, market-value revisions, site changes, litigation and ownership disputes. These are plausible non-corrupt explanations that require package-level testing. The audit excludes Phases 2A and 2B and does not establish the operational condition in October 2026. A newly published old finding cannot by itself forecast a repeated failure. Unvalidated scenario: By 5 April 2027, a publicly inspectable action-taken record establishes whether tax-basis estimation and land-readiness controls were implemented for new Phase 2 packages. Alternatives: Revised SOPs and ready land make the old sample unrepresentative. Costs reflect legitimate scope/market changes rather than an estimate defect. Falsifiers: Dated adopted controls plus a sample of new tenders demonstrate consistent tax treatment. Package records show timely land availability and no repeat compensation cause.

documents.title: Chennai smart meters: repeated tenders and a ten-year service commitment
documents.text: Do the October 2026 bid documents explain changes in coverage, lifetime cost and competition after successive cancellations? Latest reporting says TNPDCL has floated seven packages for about 1.7 crore consumers after prior revisions. The appropriate investigation is a versioned comparison of tender terms, bidders and future service payments; neither a cancelled bid nor an approved scheme budget establishes corruption. The 7 October report describes 56.85 lakh Chennai-region meters within the new programme and a separate tender for 4.72 lakh distribution-transformer meters. These are reported tender quantities, not completed installations. The same report describes earlier tender rounds in August 2023 and March 2025, subsequent revisions and cancellations. It cites low participation and high maintenance quotes in an earlier round; the August 2026 report cites unspecified irregularity allegations. A reported 10-year installation/maintenance service structure makes present purchase prices an incomplete measure of cost. Central support is reported as 15% of meter cost; the separate government-office programme involving PFC Consulting should not be merged with the seven consumer packages. September reporting puts approved RDSS outlay at ₹28,731.74 crore, including ₹19,163.5 crore for smart metering. These are scheme allocations and cannot be treated as the value of October tenders or as payments. Counterevidence: The utility's reported explanation is that smart meters reduce delayed or incorrect readings; officials expect falling meter prices. Re-tendering can produce savings and improve competition. The August account described approvals as prospective and gave different proposed coverage. October's later report changes the baseline, but only the original schedules can establish whether this reflects phased scope rather than impropriety. No winning supplier, disbursement, party donation link or personal benefit is established by these sources. The record is about procurement design and verification gaps. Unvalidated scenario: By 5 April 2027, the October consumer-meter packages have a publicly identifiable award, cancellation or revised tender, with enough terms to compare ten-year cost and bidder participation. Alternatives: Competition improves after prices fall. Scope is transparently phased and lifecycle cost declines. Falsifiers: Published evaluations show comparable bids, competition and justified lifecycle pricing. Versioned documents explain changes without preferential exceptions.

documents.title: HAL–GE: contract value, engine shipments and aircraft acceptance
documents.text: Will engine supply and certification milestones support the public delivery commitments, and are contractual delay remedies actually recovered? Original contract announcements and current named responses support a foreign-supplier dependency graph. The measurable concern is delivery and enforcement, with no evidence here of an illicit arms-dealing or personal-payment route. GE's August 2021 announcement values the 99-engine-and-support order at $716 million with overall delivery commitment by 2029. This is the first programme's engine contract, not proof of funds disbursed or an immediate deadline for all 99 engines. The second MoD–HAL contract, announced September 25 2025, covers 97 aircraft at over ₹62,370 crore excluding taxes, with deliveries beginning 2027–28 over six years. It is distinct from the first 83-aircraft programme. On October 7 2026, reporting quotes GE announcing four September shipments and describes a 14-engine tally. Shipping, HAL receipt, aircraft certification and IAF acceptance are separate milestones and must be recorded separately. The same report says HAL is imposing liquidated damages and expects 22 engines by year-end. Assessment, recovery and any waiver were not independently verified; neither damages nor supplier nationality establishes corruption. Counterevidence: HAL CMD Ravi K's September interview describes remaining radar/software standard-confirmation tests, not an engine-only explanation. His statement of ten engines received was a September snapshot, not a contradiction to later shipments. GE's reported four-engine shipment indicates progress. A programme may miss near-term milestones while still being within the overall 2029 commitment for the original engine order. The official second-tranche delivery start is 2027–28. It would be incorrect to label those 97 aircraft overdue in October 2026. Unvalidated scenario: By 31 March 2027, at least ten first-tranche Mk1A aircraft have publicly documented acceptance by the Indian Air Force. Alternatives: Recent shipments and completed tests enable delivery. A revised transparent acceptance schedule explains slippage without misconduct. Falsifiers: Public IAF acceptance records establish at least ten first-tranche deliveries by 31 March 2027, defeating the shortfall concern. Audited remedy disclosures reconcile assessed and recovered damages where due; this tests enforcement separately from the aircraft-count outcome.

documents.title: Kaleshwaram: EPC scope, supplier prices and the unresolved investigation stage
documents.text: Can package-level invoices and full installation scope reconcile the equipment-price gap identified by CAG, and what formal action has actually followed? The strongest trail compares departmental estimates with information CAG obtained from BHEL. October reporting about CBI review does not establish an FIR, while August reporting raises a separate dispute about safe operation. Financing, procurement economics and dam safety must be tested independently. For packages 6, 8, 10 and 11, CAG Table 6.2 compares ₹7,212.34 crore estimated equipment cost with ₹1,686.59 crore charged by BHEL for its supplied scope. Those amounts cover different scopes, so their difference is not automatically a loss. After allowing 30% for other operations, ₹85 crore per lift for common equipment and 20% overhead/profit on BHEL items, Table 6.3 identifies possible undue benefit of ₹2,684.73 crore. The estimate is explicitly conditional and disputed. The department told CAG that contracts did not require the supplier invoices requested for other packages. This identifies a concrete documentation control to examine, without proving hidden onward payments. The 5 October report says officials reportedly reviewed the inquiry report and legal issues following September 2025 state consent. No original CBI registration or final court outcome was inspected. The reported consent names Medigadda, Annaram and Sundilla barrages; it does not establish that the four equipment packages in this audit comparison are themselves within a registered inquiry. Counterevidence: Telangana's May and November 2023 responses cite tailor-made equipment, 31 major components, transportation/insurance, staged installation and testing, and argue audit allowances omitted relevant costs and profit. CAG explains why it rejected those objections; both positions remain visible. August reporting describes an NDSA position that pumping decisions rest with the state and CWPRS findings differing between barrages. Without the originals this is a competing account, not a safety clearance or proof that prior damage was fabricated. A reported meeting, a state consent order and an audit recommendation are different legal stages. None is a finding of individual criminal guilt. Unvalidated scenario: By 5 April 2027, an original public investigation/status or action-taken record confirms whether package-level equipment-cost reconciliation has been required or completed. Alternatives: Original scope/installation evidence reconciles the amounts. No formal inquiry has been registered despite press accounts. Falsifiers: Documented reconciliations independently substantiate the disputed scope and rates. An original judicial or agency record closes the specific cost issue on examined evidence.

documents.title: KIIFB: follow publicity invoices through each intermediary
documents.text: Can the missing lower-tier invoices and vendor-selection record reconcile the publicity cost to actual end suppliers, services and authorised project purposes? The original FY2025–26 accounts create a concrete invoice-chain investigation. A qualified audit opinion concerns ₹79.977 crore publicity documentation; separate ₹102.8855 crore programme costs are emphasis matters without modified opinions. These different findings must not be collapsed into one corruption total. Standalone auditor pp.67–68 states ₹7,997.70 lakh (₹79.977 crore) was allocated to project promotion through outsourced media arrangements and classified as direct project cost. Vendor-selection documentation did not sufficiently establish the process to the auditor. First-level invoices were available for ₹6,238.88 lakh, but the required media-house second-level invoices were not produced. For another ₹744.53 lakh, first- and second-level invoices were produced but the next provider's invoice was absent. These are distinct documentation gaps, not proof that all services were fictitious. ₹1,985.40 lakh incurred before 13 February 2026 was ratified afterward; ₹6,012.29 lakh followed the board's sanction up to 1% of project cost. The auditor acknowledged that framework while recommending activity budgets, pre-approvals and end-use certification. The two components differ by ₹0.01 lakh from the stated total; no adverse inference is made from rounding. Auditor p.71 separately draws attention to ₹614.21 lakh and ₹9,644.34 lakh infrastructure-related programme costs under government orders, expressly without modifying its opinion for those matters. October reporting identifies them as 'CM With Me' and 'Ente Keralam'. The annual report lists commercial and public-sector banking relationships, but the inspected publicity passage does not trace a particular loan drawdown to these invoices. A loan-to-publicity cash lineage remains unproven. Counterevidence: Management told the auditor that vendor selection followed due process and rates were competitive. The auditor says evidence of the amount spent was verified and relied on Media Cell receipt authentication and CEO approval; missing next-tier bills must not be rewritten as no evidence at all. KIIFB told the news outlet publicity supports brand credibility needed to raise market funds. Former vice-chair K N Balagopal said spending was within the mandate while also saying he had not seen the audit report. The separate programme costs have government-order authority and unmodified emphasis treatment. An audit qualification is a limit on assurance for specified matters, not a criminal verdict or proof of the ₹79.977 crore being stolen. Unvalidated scenario: By 5 April 2027, an official response or subsequent assurance report states whether the missing lower-tier invoices and vendor-selection documentation were produced and the specific publicity qualification resolved. Alternatives: Delayed documentation is supplied and independently matches delivered services. Competitive procurement and a lawful fundraising purpose substantiate management's explanation. Falsifiers: Auditor-reviewed invoice chains and selection records close the specified qualification. Independent service reconciliation accounts for the questioned documentation population without unexplained differences.

documents.title: Swasthya Sathi: hospital grading, insurer recoveries and scheme borrowing
documents.text: Were identified overpayments, unlevied penalties and enrolment-control weaknesses corrected after the audit reached the legislature? The newly reported audit connects the state nodal agency to hospitals, insurers and borrowing costs. It supports specific recovery and control questions, while preserving the agency's explanation for family-count differences and avoiding accusations against individual beneficiaries. For 2018–19 through 2022–23, the audit records ₹6,882.06 crore scheme expenditure. In a 50-hospital grading sample, 31 were graded too high; ₹14.48 crore excess payments were calculated for 29 of them under assurance mode between 16 July 2022 and 31 March 2023. The other two had no financial outgo. The sample cannot be projected to all hospitals. The audit says ₹31.33 crore penalties were not imposed on National, Oriental and United India Insurance companies for claims delays under the reviewed agreements. It separately identifies ₹9.78 crore refunds due from National Insurance and Bajaj Allianz. These are different obligations, not one cash loss. The nodal agency paid ₹10.85 crore interest on ₹721.95 crore loans during 2020–22, according to §1.9.2. Budget sufficiency and health-service delivery therefore need to be studied alongside provider claims. Audit records 2.43 crore enrolled families against 2.21 crore ration-card families at different 2023 dates. This is a reconciliation trigger, not a count of fake beneficiaries. Counterevidence: The nodal agency cited population growth, family splitting and ongoing Aadhaar mapping/data sanitisation. Different database dates and definitions may explain part of the gap. The audit also records actual corrective activity: February–March 2023 post-discharge audits imposed ₹11.78 crore penalties and recovered ₹8.36 crore at that snapshot. Public super-speciality hospitals were themselves under-graded in the audit, showing a system-wide grading problem rather than a simple universal private-hospital preference. Newer claims and recovery records have not been inspected. Unvalidated scenario: By 5 April 2027, a public action-taken or recovery record identifies which sampled hospital overpayments and insurer penalties were recovered, disputed or written off. Alternatives: Documented regrading and valid settlements resolve audit objections. Reconciled enrolment removes apparent duplication without reducing legitimate coverage. Falsifiers: Recovery receipts or reasoned resolutions account for the specific audit sample. New independent claims and grading checks demonstrate that the control defect has ended.

documents.title: Odisha mineral welfare: village eligibility, police vehicles and returned funds
documents.text: Can each questioned DMF allocation be reconciled to an eligible affected population, lawful purpose, sanction, payment and any repayment? September reporting on a newly tabled CAG audit links mining-derived welfare funds to stadium and police-vehicle expenditure while some directly affected villages received no DMF project. The original audit remains a priority gap; Bhubaneswar is the oversight location, not the location of all works. Reporting attributes to CAG a ₹136.77 crore Sundargarh DMF sanction for the Rourkela hockey stadium, questioned against PMKKKY purposes. The Indian Express calls this a sanction; other reports describe expenditure, so the actual disbursement stage remains to be reconciled. The Indian Express reports ₹4.63 crore released to Rourkela SP for 25 patrolling vehicles, subsequently re-deposited without ₹22.53 lakh interest. Return of principal is material counterevidence against portraying the entire release as retained money. Hindustan Times reports ₹983.32 crore expenditure in 976 non-affected villages in Keonjhar and Sundargarh, while 488 directly affected villages had no DMF-funded project during 2015–24. The classifications and overlapping totals require original records. The reported funding source is statutory contributions by mining leaseholders. This does not establish that a specific mining company controlled any beneficiary decision or received the money back. Counterevidence: The police-vehicle principal was reportedly re-deposited, so the remaining issue includes interest, authority and opportunity cost rather than an assumed unrecovered ₹4.63 crore. BJD leaders told the Indian Express they would respond after reading the report. That is a pending response, not an admission; no subsequent response or adjudication was established in this search. An asset may have public value while its funding source is impermissible. Neither construction of a stadium nor association with a police office proves private enrichment. Unvalidated scenario: By 5 April 2027, an official DMF action-taken record resolves the police-vehicle interest issue and identifies correction or justification of the questioned stadium funding. Alternatives: Funding was lawfully substituted or amounts and interest were returned. Original replies and applicable rules justify the allocation or correct its reported stage. Falsifiers: Contemporaneous rules and reasoned audit settlement establish eligibility. Certified repayment records resolve the specific principal/interest questions.

documents.title: CAG Report 7 of 2026: Bengaluru Metro Phase 1 and 2
documents.text: Audit identifies tax-inclusive estimates compared with tax-exclusive bids, land delays and debt-servicing dependence. BMRCL's replies are incorporated, including its position that bidders prepared their own estimates. §§1.3–1.4; 3.1.5; 4.2–4.3; 5.1.2; executive summary. Covers inception through March 2021, selected financial/physical progress to March 2023; excludes Phase 2A/2B. Original URL returned HTTP 503 to direct download; relevant sections inspected through a 150,000-character Exa indexed extract, not the entire PDF. Audit findings are not criminal judgments or proof of money reaching any officeholder.

documents.title: CAG announces tabling of Bengaluru Metro performance audit
documents.text: Official release dates the parliamentary tabling and reports the audit's ₹1,222.40 crore contract-cost increase calculation and March 2023 debt-service position. Dated press release, project execution and financial management sections. Same underlying audit family as the full report; not independent corroboration. Publication in 2026 does not make the audited 2023 condition a current operational fact.

documents.title: Tamil Nadu may float new bids for 56 lakh smart meters
documents.text: Unnamed utility officials describe plans for fresh tenders after cancellations and a separate government-office meter programme involving PFC. 12 August 2026 article, tender cancellation and funding paragraphs. The report describes both cancellation and a proposal awaiting board consideration; exact board order and tender IDs were not obtained. References to alleged irregularities do not establish misconduct by any bidder or minister. Prospective August plans are superseded by the October report where they conflict.

documents.title: TNPDCL floats seven smart-meter packages covering about 1.7 crore consumers
documents.text: Reports seven packages, 56.85 lakh Chennai-region meters, a separate 4.72 lakh transformer-meter tender and a 10-year service arrangement, after earlier tender revisions. 7 October 2026, 19:07 IST article; package scope, funding and earlier bid history. Original bid schedules, board approvals and awards not independently inspected. Article's package geography repeats Erode; do not reconstruct package boundaries from this prose. Tender values and winning suppliers are unknown; central support and service fees are reported terms, not observed transfers.

documents.title: HAL orders 99 F404 engines: GE original announcement
documents.text: Vendor announces a $716 million order for 99 engines and support services, with total delivery commitment by 2029. 19 August 2021 announcement, first two paragraphs. Contract announcement, not remittance evidence or a complete milestone schedule. F404 supply for the first tranche must not be merged with proposed F414 co-production or later aircraft orders.

documents.title: GE reports four September engine shipments for Tejas Mk1A
documents.text: Reports GE's statement of four September shipments, a 14-engine tally, HAL's expected 22 engines by year-end and reported liquidated damages; integration and certification work also remain. 7 October 2026 article; supplier statement, milestone and certification paragraphs. Shipping is distinct from HAL receipt, IAF acceptance and entry into service. Neither delivery delay nor an import contract proves corruption. Reported liquidated damages are not independently verified as assessed, recovered or waived.

documents.title: HAL annual report FY2024–25: Ravi K's operations role
documents.text: Official biographical disclosure states Ravi K became Director (Operations) effective November 26 2024, following Executive Director (Corporate Planning). Board biography, 'Shri Ravi K' paragraph. Historical corporate self-description; exact day the annual report was published is not verified. Relevant biography inspected in an indexed extract, not the entire report. Public role history is not evidence of personal benefit or fault.

documents.title: Kaleshwaram performance audit, Chapter VI: contract management
documents.text: Audit compares four EPC packages' pump and motor estimates with BHEL-supplied equipment costs and records Telangana's scope-comparability objections and the auditor's response. §6.2.1.1, printed pp.154–158, Tables 6.2–6.3; §6.2.1.2. Historical audit through March 2022 with government replies in May/November 2023. ₹2,684.73 crore is the audit's assumption-dependent possible undue-benefit estimate, not an adjudicated theft or observed payment to a minister. An indexed full chapter was inspected; signed contracts and supplier invoices were not independently acquired.

documents.title: CBI begins probe into Kaleshwaram project?
documents.text: Reports, citing unnamed sources, that CBI officials reviewed the PC Ghose report and legal issues; describes the state government's September 2025 consent order. Article displayed date 5 October 2026, 02:38 IST; discussion of consent and reported meeting. Headline is a question and reporting is source-based; this does not establish registration of an FIR or commencement of a formal CBI case. Search metadata uses 4 October UTC; displayed local publication date retained. Consent order, commission report and latest court docket remain acquisition gaps.

documents.title: NDSA affidavit and CWPRS report: Kaleshwaram operational debate
documents.text: Reports a position that operational pumping decisions rest with the state and that technical concerns differ between barrage components. 25 August 2026 article on NDSA affidavit and reported CWPRS examination. Politically framed account; the underlying affidavit and CWPRS report were not obtained. No engineering safety clearance can be inferred from this article. Included as a competing operational explanation, not proof that every barrage is safe.

documents.title: KIIFB discloses tendered CEO resignation, acceptance pending
documents.text: The exchange notice says K M Abraham tendered resignation under an August 18 order; acceptance was pending and the interval was to be treated as leave without pay. Letter FA-6/2027/2021/KIIFB, first page. No inferred causal relationship to the audit or allegation of personal benefit. Later government acceptance/replacement status was not verified. Original PDF SHA256 d1a3c7dbb589fb93ce5b4051bcb6289bc3bbf971f6678336f8f89909965e56f0; private-contact details not republished.

documents.title: KIIFB publicity and programme expenditure questioned after annual accounts
documents.text: Reports the accounts, critic's objections, KIIFB's stated fundraising-brand rationale and former finance minister K N Balagopal's response that spending was within the mandate. 7 October 2026 report; audit qualification and response paragraphs. Accounts are the primary source; this article is not an independent second audit. Balagopal said he had not seen the report. His response does not establish that he approved individual invoices. The ₹102.8855 crore programme-cost total is separate from the publicity qualification; do not combine them as one loss.

documents.title: KIIFB annual report and audited accounts FY2025–26
documents.text: Statutory auditor qualifies publicity documentation, while recording management's due-process explanation and verified service evidence. Separate programme costs are emphasis matters without modified opinions. PDF pp.3, 67–68 (standalone qualification), 71 (emphasis matters); consolidated equivalents pp.25–26. Original PDF SHA256 73285f74722c4cbc5b6059ef48c4c9e8a4ee57cd5853743cbcb30404917bec5a; 37,513,764 bytes. Amounts are reported in lakhs: ₹7,997.70 lakh equals ₹79.977 crore. Missing lower-tier invoices do not prove nonexistent services; the report does not identify the ultimate media recipients in the inspected passage. Ratified and later sanction components differ by ₹0.01 lakh from stated total, consistent with rounding; no adverse inference made.

documents.title: KIIFB official document and exchange-disclosure index
documents.text: Official index dates the September 7 annual report, historical December 30 2017 CEO appointment order, and subsequent exchange disclosure entries. Annual Reports tab; Government Orders; SEBI/LODR disclosures. Index is a discovery/date record, not proof of the contents of every linked disclosure. Only the annual report and August 19 CEO notice were downloaded for inspection.

documents.title: MoD signs ₹62,370 crore contract for 97 LCA Mk1A aircraft
documents.text: Official announcement of a second 97-aircraft contract, excluding taxes, deliveries starting in 2027–28 over six years. PIB Release 2171108, 25 September 2025. Contract value is not expenditure incurred or cash paid. This second tranche is distinct from the first 83-aircraft programme associated with the 2021 99-engine order.

documents.title: Mining welfare funds and excluded affected villages: Odisha CAG reporting
documents.text: Reports that ₹983.32 crore went to 976 non-affected villages while 488 directly affected villages in two districts had no DMF project during the audit period. 29 September 2026 article; district classification, project coverage and endowment findings. Same underlying CAG assertion family as the Indian Express account, despite separate reporting. No claim that lack of a DMF project means no public service from any funding source. Affected-area classification and current remediation require original district records.

documents.title: CAG flags diversion of Odisha mining welfare funds for stadium and vehicles
documents.text: Reports September 28 tabling of the 2015–24 DMF audit, including ₹136.77 crore stadium sanction, ₹4.63 crore police-vehicle release and redeposit without reported interest; BJD response is pending review. 29 September 2026 article, 'Amount re-deposited without interest' and concluding response. Original DMF audit was sought but not located for inspection; findings remain attributed reporting. Bhubaneswar is the oversight/assembly location; cited projects are in Sundargarh/Rourkela and other districts. Sanction, release, redeposit and questioned interest are distinct stages and must not be summed as stolen funds.

documents.title: HAL CMD Ravi K on LCA delays and foreign-engine negotiations
documents.text: Named management interview reports ten engines received, expected additional supply and required radar/software tests; F414 commercial negotiations remain prospective. Interview published September 17, updated September 18; engine deliveries and clearance questions. Management perspective, not independent certification. Forecasts of deliveries are claims to test, not achieved outcomes; this workbench does not adjudicate technical readiness.

documents.title: West Bengal Report 5 of 2025: Swasthya Sathi performance audit
documents.text: Audit covers ₹6,882.06 crore scheme expenditure in 2018–23 and identifies hospital grading, insurer penalties, enrolment and claims-control issues; records agency responses. §§1.8.1.2, 1.8.1.3, 1.8.1.5, 1.8.1.6, 1.9.2 and 1.11.2. Report number is 2025; newly reported tabling occurred in July 2026. Exact original publication day is unverified. Relevant sections inspected in a 150,000-character indexed extract; direct PDF download returned HTTP 503. Sample findings cannot be extrapolated to every hospital or beneficiary; a database mismatch does not identify fraudulent families.

documents.title: CAG flags Swasthya Sathi enrolment and hospital-grading breaches
documents.text: Reports the July tabling and preserves the nodal agency's explanation involving family splitting and ongoing database sanitisation. 29 July 2026 report; enrolment, response and hospital-grading sections. Derivative of the same CAG report; not an independent audit. Reports on earlier 2018–23 activity rather than current 2026 claim-level data.

documents.title: UDAY fails to revive Tamil Nadu power sector: report of CAG findings
documents.text: Reports UDAY debt-takeover shortfalls and an approved RDSS outlay of ₹28,731.74 crore, including ₹19,163.5 crore for smart metering. 8 September 2026 report on FY2024–25 State Finances Audit. Underlying current state-finance report was not retrieved; amounts remain attributed to the news account. Reported debt percentages and denominators are not reconciled here, and are not used in the case. An approved scheme outlay is not a tender award, a payment, or a loss.

documents.title: Ahmedabad police land: cancelled auction, statutory clearance and public-use value
documents.text: Was the change from commercial auction to police allocation lawfully valued and supported by a documented service need? September reporting describes Makarba plot96 reallocated for police use after a commercial sale could not be registered. The ₹38.52 crore difference is an opportunity-cost question, not evidence that anyone received that amount. Both reports identify TP84/A final plot96 and a ₹68.44 crore commercial bid versus ₹29.92 crore base value; the later report identifies Tameer Infrastructure as bidder and police as intended recipient. The earlier account says the deputy collector denied Disturbed Areas Act clearance, preventing the deed. The later account cites September 24 standing-committee approval and MLA Amit Thaker’s security representations. The reports conflict on the initial auction date; exact chronology remains held pending original municipal minutes. Counterevidence: A needed police station is a public-service asset and can justify foregoing a higher commercial bid; the public benefit must be evaluated rather than assumed to be corruption. Registration was reportedly barred by statutory permission refusal, which is an alternative explanation for cancellation independent of the later police allocation. Unvalidated scenario: Municipal or state records document completion, revision or challenge of the police allocation by evaluation date. Alternatives: Statutory refusal may lawfully block the commercial sale. Public safety benefits may exceed opportunity cost even with lower cash receipt. Falsifiers: Independent appraisal, lawful approval and measurable police-service need substantiate allocation. No private onward benefit or unauthorized change of use occurs under the registered terms.

documents.title: AMC sale cancelled after Disturbed Areas Act permission denied
documents.text: Reports the deputy collector denied permission to register the ₹68.44 crore sale under the Disturbed Areas Act, preventing completion. It records a legal-policy dispute over applying the clearance requirement to an open municipal auction. Opening paragraphs and exact TP84/A final plot96, 3,740 square metres Original refusal order and any appeal unknown. Alleged political objections are attributed to unnamed sources and not promoted to a personal-benefit edge. Same plot matched by exact scheme, plot number, size and amounts; June 2024 auction date conflicts with later report. Local publication date May 2; crawler timestamp May 1 UTC.

documents.title: Makarba commercial auction cancelled for police-station allocation
documents.text: Reports allocation of TP84/A final plot96 for police use at ₹29.92 crore instead of a ₹68.44 crore commercial bid, following MLA Amit Thaker’s security representations and prior auction cancellation. The ₹38.52 crore difference is foregone potential commercial revenue. Security demands and transaction timeline Original standing-committee resolution, deed, valuation and police payment not acquired. Public-use reallocation is not a theft finding or private transfer; opportunity-cost arithmetic is not fiscal loss adjudication. Its August 2024 auction chronology differs from Times of India’s June 2024 account; exact auction date held pending minutes.

documents.title: AEL disclosure: CG Syn-Gas & Chemicals incorporation
documents.text: AEL discloses Mundra Synenergy Limited, its wholly owned subsidiary, incorporated CG Syn-Gas & Chemicals Limited on August 23, 2025. MSEL would hold 100%; subscribed capital ₹5 lakh, turnover nil at incorporation. Page 1 opening and item a; page 2 item i; AEL CIN L51100GJ1993PLC019067 Historical incorporation snapshot, not proof of current paid-up capital, tender eligibility, later funding or total investment. No foreign investor or public loan is identified by this filing. Low initial subscribed capital by itself is not evidence of a shell or wrongdoing.

documents.title: Maharashtra afforestation: claimed utilization versus money and surviving trees
documents.text: Can state utilization claims reconcile to dated transfers, paid work and independently measured plantation survival? A newly tabled national audit and October reporting expose a testable discrepancy in historical Maharashtra scheme reporting. Mumbai denotes state oversight and Pune denotes Bhor district context; sampled works span several districts, not city-centre plantations. The 2026 publication audits 2015–16 to March 2025; it is not a claim that all sampled failures happened in 2026. The Indian Express reports ₹17.17 crore released to Maharashtra SFDA in 2018–19, ₹12.75 crore claimed utilized, ₹9.26 crore released to five FDAs and ₹0.29 crore found used. These differently scoped stages must be reconciled, not subtracted into an invented theft total. Reported Rayari (Bhor) survival was 96%, while the audit inspection reported under 5%; missing soil-moisture work and inadequate protection are measurable delivery concerns. Counterevidence: Original report records state explanations of missing matching share and overlapping committee membership; delayed funds and cattle damage can explain poor survival without proving diversion. The state reported opening a new SNA savings account from September 2021. This is a remedial claim to verify; it does not reconcile every earlier certificate. Unvalidated scenario: By evaluation date, an identifiable public corrective-action record reconciles the sampled Maharashtra utilization figures and reports a repeat survival check. Alternatives: Delayed releases and grazing damage rather than diversion may dominate. Corrective work may occur before its public record is indexed. Falsifiers: Reconciled dated ledgers show different reporting scopes account for the utilization gap. Independent site measurements and invoice reconciliation substantiate the original claims.

documents.title: Why Maharashtra’s Green India Mission saplings died: CAG lists the failures
documents.text: Reporting of CAG findings contrasts Maharashtra’s ₹12.75 crore utilization claim in 2018–19 with ₹9.26 crore released to five FDAs and ₹0.29 crore found used. It reports large survival-rate discrepancies at sampled plantations and missing soil-moisture work. Money claimed, money spent; Survival claims versus reality Financial amounts and site-level findings are reported quotations of an audit annexure not independently read in the bounded original extraction. Not an independent audit family. Article says additional chief secretary had not responded by publication. Reporter describes account opening as August 2021, whereas the original report records the department’s September 2021 SNA-account response; preserve this discrepancy.

documents.title: Audit report on Green India Mission tabled on 12 August 2026
documents.text: CAG confirms tabling date and national audit period 2015–16 to 2024–25. It reports inadequate convergence, delayed annual plans and unreliable monitoring, alongside substantial funding constraints. Opening paragraph and key audit findings Same institutional source family as report; not independent corroboration. Original bytes unavailable on direct HTTP fetch; original-URL extracted text inspected.

documents.title: CAG Report 4 of 2026: Performance Audit of Green India Mission
documents.text: Original CAG text describes weak planning, delayed transfers, unreconciled accounts and monitoring failures for 2015–16 through March 2025. Maharashtra responses cite unavailable matching share, overlapping steering-committee membership and a new SNA savings account from September 2021. §1.6.1 audit period; §2.2.2 state structure; §3.4.2 release delays; §3.11 accounts; §3.12 bank accounts Direct original PDF requests returned HTTP 503; inspected Exa extraction of original URL. Extraction is bounded and annexure-level Maharashtra amounts below are sourced to separate reporting. Publication is August 2026; underlying findings extend to March 2025 and responses to July 2025. Audit exceptions do not establish criminal intent or a diversion beneficiary.

documents.title: Goa mining FIR quashed: update the legal graph before tracing recoveries
documents.text: Which independently evidenced recovery or prosecution tracks, if any, survive the reported quashing of this specific FIR? July reports materially change the legal status of a 2013 Shah Commission-based proceeding. The investigation separates this quashed FIR from individual mining cases and any civil/statutory recoveries, rather than keeping every historical allegation active. The Goan identifies seven applicants including Salgaocar Mining Industries Pvt Ltd and reports the FIR quashed after its foundational direction was set aside. TOI reports the court cited a 2013 Supreme Court stay, lack of investigative progress and the state’s undertaking not to act solely on commission findings. ₹35,000 crore is a historical commission estimate, not a judgment fixing liability against these applicants or a traceable money transfer. Counterevidence: Defence argued the case’s foundation had fallen and prolonged prosecution was unjustified; quashing is a substantive update that defeats an unchanged active-FIR claim. A procedural quashing does not establish every separate extraction or recovery claim was false; each separate case requires its own evidence and outcome. Unvalidated scenario: By evaluation date, a court or competent Goa authority publishes a case-specific post-quashing update identifying closure, review/appeal or separately numbered surviving proceedings. Alternatives: Some recoveries may be administrative or civil and independent of the FIR. No proceedings may survive for a specific entity. Falsifiers: Certified order and subsequent registry records show no remaining proceeding for the exact case/entity. Independent records demonstrate a surviving track rests on evidence other than the invalidated foundation.

documents.title: Goa High Court sets aside mining FIR against seven firms
documents.text: Reports quashing of a 2013 FIR on the application of seven named mining firms after the Supreme Court set aside the foundational direction. ₹35,000 crore is the Shah Commission’s historical estimate, not a newly adjudicated loss. Article body and named petitioning firms Original July 2026 court order not located; precise case number and operative date remain acquisition gaps. Do not infer all Goa mining cases ended; this reported outcome concerns the specified FIR and applicants. Publisher local date July 16 differs from crawler UTC July 15; local publication date retained.

documents.title: Reported reasons: mining FIR contradicted Supreme Court stay
documents.text: Reports that the High Court cited a March 22, 2013 direction, April 30 Supreme Court stay, subsequent FIR and long lack of investigative progress. Defence argued the foundational order had fallen and prosecution was delayed. Court quotations and Salgaocar Mining Industries counsel’s submission Same underlying judicial-event family as The Goan, not two independent legal findings. Original order unavailable; reports vary on the August 2013 FIR day, so exact FIR date is not fixed here. July quashing must replace stale active-FIR labels for this proceeding, without becoming blanket exoneration for separate matters.

documents.title: Bombay High Court grants Ketan Kadam bail: documentary counterevidence
documents.text: Reports April 22 bail order finding prima facie support for Kadam’s response: no desilting contract awarded to him, third-party machines permitted, documentary evidence of procurement and allotment, and work certified by senior BMC officials. Justice R M Joshi’s April 22 observations; defence and prosecution submissions Original order not independently retrieved; news reports detailed judicial reasoning. Bail-stage observations are material counterevidence, not final acquittal; latest final trial outcome not established by inspected sources. ₹2.41 crore salary-route claim is prosecution-attributed, not independently verified or summed with alleged project loss.

documents.title: Mithi flood works: test the quantity records against the bail counterevidence
documents.text: Do source-level machinery, weighbridge and site-inspection records establish payment for work not delivered, or defeat that suspicion? October reporting describes continued desilting inquiries. The April bail court’s reported machinery and certification findings materially weaken a central prosecution premise and stay beside every related hypothesis. EOW alleges ₹65.54 crore loss and manipulation of equipment terms, rental pricing and silt quantities; admitted sources do not include the original bill-by-bill loss calculation. Reports describe BMC tender specifications matching Matprop equipment and involvement of Virgo Specialties in machine supply. These are investigation claims, not concluded collusion. October reporting says Dino Morea was questioned, not named as accused, and denied arrest. No Morea-to-minister or proceeds-beneficiary graph edge is asserted here. Counterevidence: April 22 bail reasoning reportedly found procurement and allotment documents for two machines and certification by BMC officials. It also found Kadam or his companies did not hold the desilting work contract and third-party machine provision was permitted. Defence said further custody was unnecessary after charge sheet; the judge recorded no criminal history. Neither public association nor older accusation establishes propensity. Flooding can result from rainfall, downstream bottlenecks and maintenance deficiencies; a flood event alone cannot prove false billing. Unvalidated scenario: A subsequent court, audit or procurement record explicitly resolves a disputed machinery or bill-quantity issue by evaluation date. Alternatives: Valid hired machinery and certified work can explain contractor arrangements. Quantity discrepancies may be recordkeeping errors or legally priced contingencies. Falsifiers: Machine serials, deployment logs and independent measurement match paid quantities. Final judicial findings reject the specific claim; update and retire that hypothesis.

documents.title: Mithi desilting investigation: October questioning and disputed claims
documents.text: Reports EOW examination of desilting equipment specifications, rental pricing and silt-quantity records, with ₹65.54 crore alleged loss. It reports October 2 questioning of Dino Morea, expressly says he was not named an accused, and records his denial of arrest. Tender/machinery and quantities sections; clarification of Morea’s status Agency allegations through a news explainer, not an inspected charge sheet or bank ledger. October questioning does not negate the earlier bail court’s specific findings. No edge is created from social contact, family acquaintance or unverified transaction rumours to a minister or ultimate beneficiary.

documents.title: GPPL Q4 FY2026 earnings call: royalty set-off and concession uncertainty
documents.text: CFO Santosh Breed describes present concessional waterfront royalty as a set-off against investment. MD Girish Aggarwal says future royalty or bidding arrangements are GMB’s decision and the proposed ₹17,000 crore plan is still too early to detail. Q&A with Ketan Jain; opening introduction; Q&A with Bhavesh Patel Management description, not underlying royalty accounts or concession clause. Same issuer family; parsed transcript has inconsistent Agarwal/Aggarwal spelling, not treated as two people.

documents.title: GPPL exchange disclosure: comfort letter for processing concession extension
documents.text: GPPL says it received a GMB comfort letter to process its extension proposal, requesting performance records and an investment/business plan within 90 days of the letter. It does not announce a signed extension or royalty terms. Page 1, substantive paragraphs 1–3; NSE GPPL / BSE 533248; CIN L63010GJ1992PLC018106 This is GPPL’s signed disclosure of a letter, not the complete GMB letter or amended concession. The 90-day obligation runs from the letter’s date; disclosure receipt date is August 26. Documentary processing step, not a transfer or final approval.

documents.title: APM Terminals Pipavav proposed ₹17,000 crore expansion MoU
documents.text: Company describes a ₹17,000 crore proposed expansion investment scope subject to a long-term concession agreement with GMB, within a wider Maersk investment intention. Opening paragraphs and concession condition Corporate promotional statement; proposed investment is neither disbursed public funding nor completed capex. Same issuer-side family as GPPL filing.

documents.title: Gujarat’s port reforms at crossroads
documents.text: Reports Pipavav concession expiry September 29, 2028 and Mundra February 16, 2031, earlier extension requests and investment-horizon tradeoffs. Notes that differing state concessions may expressly allow longer extensions. In a limbo; Evolving sector Concession agreements and earlier extension applications not independently acquired. Comparable longer concessions are context, not proof Gujarat must adopt identical terms.

documents.title: Gujarat port concession rollover report and named official responses
documents.text: Reports possible rollover for Mundra, Pipavav, Hazira and Dahej. Named GMB chief Ajay Kumar said on August 19 no decision had yet been taken; ports secretary Hareet Shukla said policy precedes structure. Investment-recovery concerns explain the commercial case for extensions. Named August 19 responses and discussion of initial 30-year concessions Unnamed-source rollover claim cannot supersede the precise August 26 comfort-letter disclosure. No final concession duration, price or competitive benchmark supplied.

documents.title: Gujarat port concessions: comfort letter, renewal price and investment obligations
documents.text: Will renewal terms transparently value public waterfront rights and bind the operator’s promised investment? An original August 26 filing advances the Pipavav extension process but stops short of final renewal. The investigation compares public asset terms, existing royalty set-offs and proposed private investment; the port itself is at Pipavav, with Gandhinagar policy and Mumbai corporate-disclosure context. GPPL disclosed a comfort letter requiring performance and investment/business documents within 90 days of the letter; neither tenure nor royalty terms were announced. ₹17,000 crore is a proposed expansion investment scope conditional on a long-term concession, not money paid to Gujarat. Management describes existing royalty concessions as investment set-offs; the exact investment credit and future treatment need contract-level verification. Reports place Pipavav expiry in September 2028 and Mundra in February 2031; final agreement documents are needed before calling any transfer permanent. Counterevidence: Long-payback port investment creates a legitimate reason for extension discussions; reported extensions elsewhere sometimes arise from express contract provisions. Named GMB chief said no decision had been taken on August 19. Later disclosure supports processing progress, not the broader claim that all four renewals were completed. Unvalidated scenario: GPPL or GMB publishes a subsequent concession-processing disclosure identifying submission, decision or final terms by evaluation date. Alternatives: Time needed for appraisal may legitimately delay a decision. A competitive process or shorter conditional extension may replace rollover. Falsifiers: Disclosed terms show independent valuation, public-return protection and enforceable investment obligations. Operator receives no extension and its existing term remains unchanged.

documents.title: Shivpuri defence manufacturing: announced capex versus financing and public support
documents.text: Which legal project entity, funding instruments and public support conditions will underwrite the announced investment? The July 5 company filing announces ₹2,500 crore planned defence manufacturing capex and forecast jobs. This is an ongoing project-monitoring case from just outside the latest window, with no established impropriety and no evidence here of a government purchase award. Company announced groundbreaking July 5, 2026 and planned ₹2,500 crore investment with forecast 5,000 direct/indirect jobs. Neither figure is verified expenditure or delivered employment. A separate news report describes an approximately three-year operational target; underlying milestone agreement remains unavailable. The public release names political office holders and company leadership attending or endorsing the project. Attendance is recorded as public context, not as a financial relationship. Counterevidence: Indigenous supply-chain development, domestic employment and industrial capability are stated legitimate objectives. A private defence investment announcement is not itself a procurement irregularity. No admitted source establishes the project’s exact SPV, public subsidy, concessional land price, foreign equity, secured lender or an armed-forces order. These remain acquisition gaps, not hidden-money findings. Unvalidated scenario: Within 180 days, at least one identifiable public financing, project-entity or statutory-approval milestone becomes available for the announced Shivpuri project. Alternatives: Ordinary private finance and standard industrial approvals may explain the project completely. A long construction schedule can produce limited near-term financial disclosure. Falsifiers: Exact-entity financing and support records reconcile to ordinary disclosed terms with no unexplained public concession. Announcement is revised or delayed and no public payment has occurred.

documents.title: AEL exchange filing: ₹2,500 crore Shivpuri defence investment announcement
documents.text: AEL forwards its company release announcing a ₹2,500 crore Shivpuri defence manufacturing project and forecast 5,000 direct/indirect jobs. Groundbreaking is July 5, 2026; the statement describes planned domestic defence-production capability. Page 1 exchange cover; enclosed July 5 company media release Historical baseline: July 5 is two days before the latest discovery window. Planned private capex and projected jobs are not public payments, purchase orders, expenditure certification or completed output. The release identifies a business arm, not the exact project SPV, land lessee or borrower.

documents.title: Adani Defence & Aerospace Shivpuri groundbreaking release
documents.text: Company release names Mohan Yadav, Jyotiraditya Scindia and Jeet Adani in public project roles and describes the industrial capability and jobs rationale. No public subsidy, land price, defence purchase price or award is disclosed. Opening, public statements and project background Same release enclosed in exchange filing; one source family, not independent confirmation. Public-event attendance and welcoming an investment do not establish procurement authority, ownership or private benefit. No sensitive operational information is extracted; case concerns financing/governance records only.

documents.title: Shivpuri defence plant: reported three-year operational target
documents.text: Reports a three-year target to become operational, covering land development, construction, installation, workforce and certification. It attributes this timetable to an official release and describes the employment/MSME rationale. Timeline and production roadmap News account of an official timetable; underlying state release and milestone financing plan not acquired. No progress update dated July 7–October 7 independently established. Three-year target is not a signed delivery guarantee.

documents.title: Tara revised coal block: ownership, boundary change and clearance gates
documents.text: Does the revised auction boundary and clearance record resolve the earlier ecological objections before any extraction begins? September official and opposition statements disagree on the consequences of reopening Tara. An original company filing establishes the CG Syn-Gas → Mundra Synenergy → Adani Enterprises ownership chain as a separate branch; the reported auction-winner name is held unmerged until the exact award identity is verified. Raipur is the state decision hub; the mine is in Hasdeo-Arand. PIB says the block was removed in July 2023, reintroduced after a December 11, 2025 state letter and CMPDIL boundary revision, with nine bids and a 37.50% revenue-share result. The company’s August 23, 2025 filing documents MSEL as AEL’s wholly owned subsidiary and its incorporation of CSGCL with 100% holding and ₹5 lakh subscribed capital. This is historical capitalization, not project financing. ₹1,200 crore annual revenue and over 8,000 jobs are Ministry projections; this archive does not represent them as received money or verified employment. The reported winner and incorporated company have closely similar names, but this graph does not merge them. The award/CIN match is a visible missing identity hop. Counterevidence: Government says the revised block excludes the Lemru corridor influence zone and no tree felling/mining may begin before statutory approvals. These are concrete claims to test against GIS and clearance orders. Opposition forest-loss figures and allegations of political favoritism are not independently measured or established by the materials admitted here. A newly incorporated project subsidiary and small initial capital can be normal project structuring; eligibility and parent-support terms, not incorporation alone, decide financing adequacy. Unvalidated scenario: Within 180 days, a publicly identifiable statutory-clearance or consultation milestone is issued for Tara Revised with its exact revised boundary. Alternatives: Project can be delayed or refused on ecological grounds. Boundary change may materially reduce the disputed impact. Falsifiers: Versioned independent GIS and clearance reasoning resolve corridor concerns. No physical work occurs before requisite approvals and conditions are independently complied with.

documents.title: CMDC: Tara auction completed, mining awaits statutory clearances
documents.text: CMDC identifies CG Syn & Gas and Chemicals Limited as winner and says mining, forest and environmental approvals remain prerequisites to tree felling or extraction. The statement provides earlier allocation and policy context. CMDC statement on award, clearance sequence, 2011 allocation and earlier state correspondence News reproduction of a government statement; not an independently downloaded allocation order. Statement’s scientific-study characterization is not independently verified against original ICFRE report. The reported bidder spelling differs from the original incorporation filing. It is held as a separate source-mention node; no legal-identity bridge is asserted without the award order or CIN match.

documents.title: Jairam Ramesh objects to Tara coal-block auction
documents.text: Reports an opposition challenge based on the 2022 assembly resolution, 2023 state exclusion request and claimed forest/corridor impacts. This frames an environmental-policy dispute for comparison with the Ministry’s revised-boundary response. Changed policy; ownership section; forest-impact claims Opposition allegations, not independent ecological measurement or proof of political corruption. Tree-count and acreage claims not promoted as independently measured facts; original resolution, affidavit and GIS evidence still needed.

documents.title: Facts on Auction of Tara (Revised) Coal Block
documents.text: Ministry says Tara was excluded in July 2023, reconsidered after Chhattisgarh’s December 11, 2025 request and boundary revision by CMPDIL, attracted nine bids and was auctioned at 37.50% revenue share. ₹1,200 crore annual revenue and over 8,000 jobs are projections. All substantive paragraphs, especially December 2025 letter and revised boundary Official explanation needs testing against actual letter, geospatial boundary versions and technical-evaluation record. Projected revenue is not a receipt; nine submitted bids alone does not prove nine independent qualified competitors.
